T 1.0: 155/328 with 100 neurons zeroed and 130 with 1,000, against 164 unedited (identical requests there range 155 to 168); cap hits 77 -> 47 and 32, tokens 9,344 -> 8,706 and 8,556. T 0.6: 149 and 149 (24 and 6 loops; unedited T 0.6 cell running). The edit turns cap hits into finished wrong answers, as result-51fd20 found for forced commits. Closing this line for the scoreboard: loops and 17-26 % of tokens go at T 0.6, right answers do not rise. xreward trace (forward pass, base model on its own 328 hard328 answers, 1,572,055 positions, job abaybektursun-1115-005830-2145): the base's MLP inputs drive the 8 input directions of the Math 3.1 difference 8.1 to 11.2 times more than a random subspace with the same singular values (by layer band); Code 3.1's 6.3 to 8.9 times; IF's 2.0 to 4.5 times. So the top-8 input subspaces sit on directions that math-solution text really excites, more for the reasoning rewards than for IF: support for reading the input-side overlap of result-9d979a as a trace of the text a run generated. The edit changes each matrix's output by under 0.6 %. Nulls: drive does not differ between cap-hit and finished answers (ratio 0.99 to 1.01); at Wait/Hmm/perhaps positions it is 1.22x other positions but So/Therefore/Then is 1.17x, so the check-specific excess is 5 to 10 %, and Code 3.1 shows the same. No cap hit has a loop onset by rule A or B at T 1.0. Caveat: bootstrap intervals pool positions and are too narrow. Artifacts studies/rlneurons/results/xreward/trace-01/readout.json, spec specs/SPEC_xreward_trace.md, branch sharedsub.

title: Budget of the cued-base-to-RL gap in four cells: loops replace reliability at T 0.6
what: Fixed rules sort each problem the RL model solves and the cued base misses into loop, budget (cap hit), answer statement, reliability (base right in another stored row) or capability.
why: It shows where the gap sits; at T 1.0 a fresh base sample's gap has RL's budget.
caveat: Gross gaps, one sample per side; hard328 evidence rows weaker (T 0.6, v1); T 0.6 cell graded v1.
Shares (n; loop/budget/answer/reliability/capability; 3 evidence rows): MATH-500 T 1.0 RL 65: 0/.25/.03/.63/.09; theta0.5 53: 0/.21/.04/.64/.11; hard328 Code-RL 37: 0/.27/.03/.43/.27; step 400 T 0.6 66: .44/.12/.06/.38/0; base resample 42: 0/.17/.02/.67/.14. Apart at 90 %: only T 0.6 loop, reliability, capability against each MATH-500 T 1.0 cell, and hard328 capability against RL. Surprise: T 0.6 reliability .38, predicted .15; 9 of its 25 are right answers v1 rejects. studies/theory/results/account/run-02/readout.md (branch theory, a92ae63 and later)

Theory round 05, refuted theories (each by a number computed from stored rows; studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/metrics_v4.json): (1) grader v3 false negatives explain part of the hard328 gap: numeric equivalence recovers 0 of the cued base's finished v3-wrong non-integer answers, gap stays 12.8 points. (2) the cued base overwrites a right first answer: 0 of its v3-wrong MATH-500 answers have a right first marker. (3) base wrong samples are shorter than right siblings on Levels 1-3: they are longer, median log ratio +0.193. (4) the base restates after 'Wait' while RL re-derives: both revise at the same rate, ratio 1.04. (5) Think-SFT fails by cap hits on RL's longest problems: 25 cap hits of 500, and it is 6 problems ahead of RL in the longest quartile. (6) RL step 100 opens with the RL cue: 3.4 % of plain T 0.6 answers open with 'line'. (7) the base boxes a number from the problem statement: base minus RL share -0.043. (8) Code-RL 3.1 wins by code-style work: markers no more frequent than in the cued base, marked answers 0.123 less accurate. (9) RL-only problems are ones the base solves 'a few percent' of the time: per-sample rate is 0.237. (10) Code 3.0 loses long problems through cap hits: 5 cap hits of 500. (11) nothing after the opening adds to the cue's gain: see idea-2f32ff.

title: Theory round 05 computed these numbers from stored rows
what: Tests written by theories before any row was read; the two no-theory readers did not expect the first three.
why: They locate the Code 3.0 deficit by answer length and show the base already solves most RL-only problems sometimes.
MATH-500, T 1.0, grader v3, one run, not recomputed independently. (a) Code 3.0 cue against Code 3.1 cue: 0.795 of Code 3.1's lead lies in the longest quartile by RL answer length; on the shorter half Code 3.0 has 246 right and Code 3.1 243 of 250 (readers expected Code 3.1 ahead by 10 to 15); against the cued base Code 3.0 is +7.25 problems on the shorter half and -11.25 in the longest quartile. Cause open: Code 3.0 has 5 cap hits of 500, so it is not the cap. (b) Of the 17 problems RL solves and the cued base missed 4 of 4, fresh independent base samples solve 11 at least once (0.647), per-sample rate 0.237; of the 16 that RL also misses, 0.522 fewer. (c) base+top8 plain has 22 quick finished-wrong answers (at most 2,000 tokens; readers 8 and 9). Artifacts: studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/tests/r5-m08.json, studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/tests/r5-m06.json, studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/tests/r5-m03.json, studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/examples.json

title: Signed self-training with no reward loses points
what: One LoRA epoch on the base's 4 stored samples per MATH-500 problem, raising the samples that agree with the vote and lowering the others (arm P), or the same with the answer key (arm G), then the cue on hard328 (n 328, T 1.0, v3, 1 sample).
why: RL's update is signed; SFT on voted samples was not. Neither the sign nor the key helps offline: answers stop finishing (cap hits 77 -> 178 / 145, no loops, Wait doubles); where both finish, accuracy is equal.
caveat: one epoch, stored samples only, no resampling. Held-out NLL gap wrong-minus-right did not rise.

title: Entropy-gated temperature does not beat plain T 1.0
what: Base + cue on MATH-500: T 0.6 only at confident positions (entropy <= 0.9 nats), only at forks, or everywhere except after a repeat. All three score 1.3 to 1.4 points under plain T 1.0 (410.5/500), intervals through 0.
why: Cap hits per 500: T 1.0 22.5, forks only 33, confident only 44, both (T 0.6) 98; adding the two gives 55, so loops need both regimes sharpened. Removing randomness trades accuracy of finished answers for loops. Not run on the 328.
caveat: T 0.6 is one stored sample; the repeat-aware cell has 1 sample (the second was lost in a box teardown); score lines round the means 403.5 to 404. Intervals: -1.4 [-3.2, 0.4], -1.4 [-3.5, 0.8], -1.3 [-4.3, 1.5].
Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/README.md section 'Entropy-gated temperature', results/egate/ (main). About 17 USD vast.ai.

Literature for 'RL first installs the cue's opening' and for label-free RL, read 2026-11-15 (findings in tools/paper.py). (1) Per-checkpoint cue curve is unpublished: 2610.24663 Table 3 scores a one-token opening only on base and final RL (Qwen3-4B-Base, AIME: 10.00 -> 13.23, RL 19.32, 35 % of the gain); 2610.06851 App. D Fig. 14 trains RL with the cue forced (reaches plain RL's step-300 accuracy in 100 steps) and Fig. 16 gives opening probabilities before and after RL only. No paper scores plain and cued prompts, or the opening's probability, at intermediate checkpoints of plain RL. (2) Vote-reward RL from a base model is published, without token matching: 2511.04902 Table 1, MATH-500, Qwen2.5 base: 7B 58.2 -> vote 73.6 vs labelled 73.8; 3B 54.2 -> 63.8 vs 64.4; 0.5B collapses to 0.0 vs 33.8. TTRL 2504.16084: Qwen2.5-7B 60.5 -> 80.5. So a no-label reward equals a labelled one when the start model is right often enough, and fails when it is not. (3) Tinker (Thinking Machines) serves no Olmo model; its base models are Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B-Base and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base; its cookbook RL loop defaults to the 9B base, LoRA rank 32, lr 4e-5. A ready study for the per-checkpoint curve there (spec, RL loop with grader or vote reward, eval, readout, offline run passed, no model call yet) is on branch tinker, studies/tinkerpair/specs/SPEC.md; it waits on account billing. idea-035a30

Grader v3 scores an 'Answer:' line wrong when an algebraic answer ends with a period ('15x - 80.' against gold '15x - 80'; numbers and $..$. are accepted). Size, counted on committed MATH-500 rows by regrading with the period removed: base cue 4 samples 0 of 2,137 rows, RL 4 samples 1 of 2,041 ('√53.'), egate hi6 1 of 1,000, lo6 2 of 2,000, esc3k 0 of 500. At most 0.1 point in any cell and no base-against-RL bias, so no posted number changes; a grader v5 is not worth a rescore for this alone. Found while reviewing result-34897a.

title: RL's top directions make the model finish, not be right
what: Added 1, 8 or 64 top singular directions per matrix of (RL-Math minus base) to the base, at 1x and 2x size, by module family and split by Code 3.0's input subspace; scored on 328 hard problems with the cue.
why: Cap hits follow the size of the 8 directions: RL minus them 90, base 77, one direction 51, eight 46, eight at 2x 5. Right answers per finished answer stay near 0.65 (0.59 at 2x).
caveat: One sample per cell; contrasts under about 5 points are not resolved. Edited cells carry BF16 rounding noise that base and RL do not.
xreward second batch (hard328 n 328, cue, T 1.0/top-p 1.0, v3, seed 3000000). Rank curve: rand8 158, base 164, k=1 181, k=8 192, k=64 200 (0.115% of weight norm; -1.8 pts vs RL [-5.5, 1.8]), RL 206. Attention only 178, MLP only 181 (diff +0.9 [-3.0, 4.9]): no module family carries it. 2x scale: 190 right, 5 cap hits (predicted 195-206: refuted); on the base's 77 cap-hit problems it finishes all, 14 right, 63 wrong. Control: RL minus random rank-8 195 right / 33 cap hits vs RL minus top-8 190 / 90: the accuracy loss is not separable from perturbation, the cap hits are the 8 directions. Shared-input split refuted: part in Code 3.0's input subspace 171, rest 176. Code 3.0's own 8 directions: 173 right, 23 cap hits. Artifacts: branch sharedsub, studies/rlneurons/results/xreward/edits/readout.json and run folders, README section xreward.
